cameraV2.claim: Camera interpolation searches the previous and next key that actually carries the requested property (sparse keyspans); the two lookup routines are FUN_1401e3870 (previous) and FUN_1401e3690 (next). Each property checks its own flag bit.

Camera key array stride is 0x380 bytes; key entry stride 0xE0: frame +0x00, rotation +0x18 (double), zoom +0x20 (double), sizeX +0x28 (double), sizeY +0x30 (double), flags +0x48 (bit1 rotation, bit2 zoom, bit3 size), per-property ease curves +0x178 (zoom), +0x238 (rotation), +0x2F8 (position). Therefore key x/y are the camera frame SIZE, not a pan offset.

FUN_1401da730 builds the camera rectangle from evaluated size, zoom and rotation, returns corners in TL, TR, BR, BL order, and uses the path point as centre when one exists; otherwise falls back to the scene/camera centre.
FUN_14081ec20 rasterises the ease curve into 1001 uint16 samples; sampling is x-mirrored at table build time. The linear default therefore still behaves as a standard ease.
Blend between keys A and B is c = clamp01(B.curve(1 - t)); value = A*(1-c) + B*c, i.e. the later key's curve is evaluated with 1-t, in all four evaluators (x, y, zoom, rotation).
tv_camerainfoframe prints six doubles in the order pathX, pathY, rotation, zoom*100, sizeX, sizeY. The argument setup and the six-float format string were read at 0x1403f143f..0x1403f1500.
Path points between keyed positions are interpolated linearly in our implementation; the original path evaluator FUN_1401e2690 (~17.9 KB) was not fully decoded.
Zoom is applied at the same composition stage as the corner geometry (scale before rotation/translation). The exact compositor matrix application point is not confirmed.

timelineInstances.claim: tv_exposureinfo/break/add/set/next/prev/fauxfixe are real script commands. Their name strings live at 0x140a62268..0x140a622d0 and the name/handler pairs are 16 bytes apart starting at 0x140a5ff60: info->0x14040ddc0, break->0x14040dc50, add->0x14040dbe0, set->0x14040df60, next->0x14040dec0, prev->0x14040df10, fauxfixe->0x14040dcc0.

A layer's timeline is image INSTANCES with exposure counts, not start/end strips. tv_exposureinfo prints 'Exposure %d %d' with the value from FUN_14078de00 and a constant 0, or an empty string when FUN_14078dfd0 says the frame has no image. FUN_14078dfd0/FUN_14078de00 dispatch on layer type (layer+0x2c = 1/2/4/5/8) and FUN_1404a7e40(container, frame - layerStart) resolves the value, so held frames share the image.

tv_exposureset calls FUN_1407b3100(frame, n): frame -999999 means the current scene frame (scene+0x48); the frame is range-checked against FUN_14078ce20/FUN_14078e200 (layer first/last frame); a flag at layer+0x20 bit4 short-circuits; n is clamped to >= 1; for image layers the instance containing the frame is grown (insert instances) or shrunk (remove instances), which is exactly what our runs model does.

tv_exposurebreak calls FUN_14068f700, which allocates an undo command object of RTTI class cMUDBreakInstances (.?AVcMUDBreakInstances@@ at 0x140cddbd0) holding the layer and the frame, then FUN_14078aa30. So 'break' is a first-class undoable instance split, not a strip edit.

tv_layerprebehavior / tv_layerpostbehavior read layer+0x6c and layer+0x70; mode values map to strings (0 -> none string referenced at DAT_140a5c96c, 1 -> 'repeat', 2 -> 'pingpong', 3 -> 'hold'). Setters go through FUN_1400d5750 / FUN_1400d54f0. These are the before/after-layer range rules our sampler implements.

Per-layer animation flags are: auto break instance = type2 sub-object +0x28 and type5 sub-object +0xb0 (getter FUN_14078a070, setter FUN_1407a31b0, folder layers recurse via FUN_1407932d0(...,1)); auto create instance = type2 +0x29 and type5 +0xb1 (getter FUN_14078a110, folder via FUN_1407932d0(...,2)). Commands tv_layerautobreakinstance / tv_layerautocreateinstance expose them and accept on/off/toggle.

Correction to an easy mistake: tv_layerhold is NOT an exposure-hold command. Its handler FUN_14040d630 builds a 'Hold&Fetch' selection tool buffer (FUN_140253920). Exposure holding is done with tv_exposureset/add.

The tv_layer command table sits at 0x140a5fc20 (16-byte name/handler pairs). Handlers relevant to the timeline/canvas: tv_layerdensity 0x140410e90, tv_layerdisplay 0x140410f40, tv_layerrecomputeexposure 0x140412f40, tv_layerinsertimage 0x1404118f0, tv_layerimage 0x14040bc80, tv_layergetimage 0x14040bc40, tv_layerblendingmode 0x14040f310, tv_layerautobreakinstance 0x14040e620, tv_layerautocreateinstance 0x14040e870, tv_layerprebehavior 0x140412ce0, tv_layerpostbehavior 0x140412a80, tv_layerhold 0x14040d630.

tv_layerrecomputeexposure (handler 0x140412f40) takes 4 arguments and either calls FUN_1400dd1a0(layer, start) or FUN_1400dcf50(layer, start, count, value) to re-space exposures over a range. The exact re-spacing curve was not decoded (we do not implement recompute).

The body of cMUDBreakInstances (its vftable) was not read, so we clone the held image into the new key (seed + recorded strokes) — which is the behaviour the UI needs and matches the visible result. Exact pointer re-use vs deep copy in the original is UNKNOWN.

keyframes.claim: The captured keymap distinguishes two navigations: Ctrl Left = PrevInstance and Ctrl Right = NextInstance (adjacent image instance), while Page Up = LayerPrevKey and Page Down = LayerNextKey (exposure boundary of the current layer). Our app implements both on those exact chords.

A key is the first frame of an image instance (offset 0 within a run) and a held exposure frame is not a key; boundaries are instance starts and end+1, because that is what the exposure setter splits on. Derived from the confirmed exposure model.

Drawing on a held frame splits the instance when auto-break is on and drawing on an empty frame creates one when auto-create is on; the flags are confirmed, the wiring of the flags into the paint path was not traced frame-by-frame.

canvas.claim: tv_layerdensity (handler 0x140410e90) reads the layer opacity as a 0..1 double (FUN_1400daaf0) and sets it from the command value / 100 (FUN_1400e3f70); the old value is returned as an integer percent. Our layer opacity uses the same 0..1 range.

tv_layerblendingmode (handler 0x14040f310) exists and sets a per-layer blend mode; FUN_1407374b0 aliases mode 0xD to 0xC, and the mode NAME list is a runtime string array (DAT_140cc0f10) that gets a 'Transparent' entry for folder layers (FUN_140737670). config.ini ships 'blendingmode=Multiply' plus blendbackground/blendmask keys, so Multiply is a real mode value in this install.

The exact number, order and integer ids of all blend modes were not recovered (the list is built at runtime). Our select offers normal/multiply/screen/add/overlay/darken/lighten/difference and maps them to Canvas2D composite operations; Multiply is the mode value confirmed from config.ini.

The paint engine internals are proprietary and were not decoded. Our brush stamps radial-gradient dabs along the stroke with pressure-driven width and alpha, spacing = 12% of the dab width, plus a replayable stroke list per image for undo. Layers composite with opacity + blend, and each instance owns its own canvas image.

Image-level script commands exist: tv_layerinsertimage 0x1404118f0, tv_layerimage 0x14040bc80, tv_layergetimage 0x14040bc40 (handlers from the tv_layer table). They are the binary's own way to reach the per-layer image, which supports the per-instance canvas model.

penPressure.claim: The string 'pressure' exists at 0x140a3d1a8 and the literal "\thas pressure ? %s\n" at 0x140a70f30, used in FUN_14053f9e0.
RTTI class .?AUcMyTabletReader@nInk@@ at 0x140cdb4e8 places the tablet/pressure reader in the ink module; globals 0x140ce0d88 and 0x140ce0d94 hold pressure state; a _pressure.mot resource exists.

Our brush maps pen pressure to width through the same style of curve object (width = size * curve(pressure), mouse = full width). The original per-brush dab spacing / texel compositing is proprietary and not reproduced.

verification.claim: npm test runs 38 Node tests covering camera v2, shortcuts parsing/serialisation/conflicts, the instance/exposure timeline model (set/add/break, auto create/break, instance-vs-key navigation, pre/post behaviours, empty exposures), and pressure-to-width; all pass.

An automated Chrome DevTools Protocol check (tools/verify-ui.mjs, no extra dependencies) drives the shipped demo like a user: it paints strokes with real mouse events, verifies auto-break split a 60f exposure into 19+41 at frame 20 with the new key cloned from the held image, undoes with Ctrl Z, exercises + Exposure / + Instance / Clear plus undo, checks Ctrl Right vs Page Down navigation, per-key canvas identity, Ctrl K (283 captured bindings) and Escape, and the camera view. 24/24 checks pass with zero console/page errors; screenshots in evidence/ui/.
